name: Katalyst

hlido_opinion.headline: A focused AI sales agent that keeps Salesforce current and preps reps for calls — named enterprise references and a real security posture, thin on programmatic openness.
hlido_opinion.body: Katalyst picks one painful, well-understood job — the CRM-hygiene and call-prep drudgery that eats a B2B rep's day — and builds an agent squarely around it: summarise every meeting/email/call, keep Salesforce deal fields updated automatically, surface buying signals (leadership moves, hiring, filings), draft context-aware follow-ups, and assemble account plans. The focus is the strength; this is not another general chatbot. Two things lift it above the pack of AI-sales tools on the public surface: the testimonials name real people at real companies (AEs at Atlassian, Stripe, Justworks), which is stronger social proof than anonymous quotes, and the page states an explicit SOC 2 posture with ISO 27001-aligned controls — the security signals procurement actually asks for. Where it is weaker: the quantified metrics (3.5x, +250%) are vendor-reported with no methodology; several integrations are marked 'coming soon'; and there is no public API, SDK, or MCP surface, so from an agent-to-agent standpoint Katalyst is a closed SaaS you use, not a component other agents can drive.

tier_rationale: STEADY (73) for a tightly-scoped, credible sales-agent product with named enterprise references and an explicit SOC 2 / ISO 27001-aligned security posture. Not higher because the impact metrics are vendor-reported without methodology, several integrations are still "coming soon", and there is no programmatic (API/SDK/MCP) surface for agent-to-agent use.
what_it_does_well: Sharp single focus: automate Salesforce hygiene and call prep rather than being a general assistant
Named testimonials from AEs at recognizable enterprises (Atlassian, Stripe, Justworks) — above-average social proof
Explicit security posture stated (SOC 2, ISO 27001-aligned controls) — the signals procurement looks for
Concrete feature set: meeting/email summarisation, signal detection, account plans, follow-up drafting
Integrates with common sales stack (CRM, email, calendar, meeting recorders)
what_it_fails_at: Headline metrics (3.5x automation efficiency, +250% pipeline hygiene) are vendor-reported with no disclosed methodology
Several stack integrations are labelled "coming soon", so current coverage is narrower than the grid implies
No public API, SDK, or MCP server — not usable as a component in an agent-to-agent workflow
Security claims are self-asserted on the page; no linked report or third-party attestation surfaced
best_for: B2B sales teams standardized on Salesforce that lose rep hours to CRM updates and call prep
Sales leaders who want cleaner pipeline data for forecasting
Orgs that require a stated SOC 2 / ISO-aligned posture from vendors
not_recommended_for: Teams not on Salesforce (the product is Salesforce-centric)
Buyers who need independently verified ROI before committing
Agent developers wanting a programmatic/API-drivable sales component
red_flags: Quantified outcome claims (3.5x, +250%) are vendor-reported without methodology — treat as marketing, not measured results
